TN-2025-SB1748.aiSummary: As enacted, this law changes rules for commercial drivers who cannot read and speak English well enough to handle road signs, public questions, and required reports. It lets officers issue an out-of-service order during a safety check, suspends the driver’s commercial license, and requires a state test before the license can be reinstated, with some exceptions for drivers who cannot meet a hearing standard but have an exemption. The employer is liable for fines and fees, and the law takes effect for most purposes on January 1, 2027.

TN-2025-SB539.aiSummary: As enacted, the law sets rules for how multi-unit rental housing with government low-income use limits is assessed for property tax. It tells assessors how to value this housing, including how to treat rent limits and low-income housing tax credits. Owners must tell the property assessor when the property is covered by these limits, when that status ends, or when foreclosure starts. These rules take effect January 1, 2026, for most purposes, with some parts taking effect when the law became effective.

TN-2025-HB2649.aiSummary: For Bristol, the law updates how city council and school board members are chosen so all city voters can vote for all seats, with some seats tied to districts and others open to any city resident. It also shortens the time for new ordinances to take effect from 17 days to 7 days, changes the city’s property tax due dates, and sets up a city department of education. The changes affect Bristol city government, the board of education, property owners, and residents who vote in city elections.

For state police officers and some Tennessee Bureau of Investigation agents, that credit must be free to the worker if they apply on or after July 1, 2026.
